contract.requires:
The source is an exclusion network with at most one particle per site, vacancy-limited hopping and accessible reservoir contacts. The symmetric reference has local memory s_i(t)=[exp(-(L+R)t)1]_i, the backward-walker survival before reservoir absorption. Here L is the reference transport Laplacian and R the reservoir-rate operator, not the global exit-rate ceiling of a different endpoint-simulator theorem. Hidden bulk may have no reservoir refresh. The transport class and closure-defect guarantee remain externally warranted premises.

Retained reservoir probe:
At each trial choose a fresh fair sign Z, set accessible reservoir densities to 1/2+aZ while preserving their total exchange rates, hold controls fixed for tau and read binary local occupancy Y_i. Both possible signs start from the same carried hidden state; only the realized branch is run. In the symmetric case E[Z(2Y_i-1)|entire history]=2a(1-s_i(tau)). No reset, stationary start or copied physical branch is used. For directed exclusion the nonlinear residual has width h_i=sum_j |(q_ij-q_ji)/2|. Under h_i<=eta*r_i, E[Z(2Y_i-1)|history]<=(2a+eta)(1-s_i(tau)). Binary score transformation and binomial stochastic domination handle dependent trials; exact integer tail inversion gives an upper confidence bound S_i.

Allowed fixed-control transfer:
For the source admissible defect/control contract, every allowed fixed combination of additional source injections obeys |E_x X_i(t)-rho_i^u|<=eta+(1-eta)S_i for t>=tau. Source strengths remain reproducible, probes preserve exchange kinetics and controls remain fixed within each sampling interval. Baseline and isolated-control observations then enclose later joint stationary means through the source retained intervention-composition construction. This is local-mean control, not arbitrary feedback or the full hidden-state law.

source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The principle constructed

I concentrated on this question:

> Can accessible interventions experimentally certify that a local prediction has become insensitive to an unknown hidden initial state?

The answer is **yes within a specified class of interacting transport systems**.

The source is an exclusion network: each site holds at most one particle, particles hop into vacancies, and a few accessible ports exchange particles with reservoirs. The hidden bulk can have no reservoir refresh at all.

For the symmetric reference dynamics, let

\[
s_i(t)=\left[e^{-(L+R)t}\mathbf 1\right]_i.
\]

This is the survival probability of a backward reference walker before absorption at a reservoir. It also bounds how much the mean occupancy at port \(i\) can retain its initial condition. The underlying absorbing-walk and exclusion machinery is established; it is not itself a new discovery. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

The constructive operation is to choose a fresh fair sign \(Z\), change the accessible reservoir densities to \(1/2+aZ\) while preserving their total exchange rates, wait a fixed time \(\tau\), and read the local occupancy \(Y_i\). In the symmetric case,

\[
\mathbb E[Z(2Y_i-1)\mid\text{entire preceding history}]
=2a[1-s_i(\tau)].
\]

The two possible signs start from the same carried hidden state. Randomization cancels that unknown initial contribution in expectation. **No reset, stationary-start preparation or copied physical branch is needed.**

I then strengthened the construction to tolerate bounded failure of mean closure. For directed exclusion, the exact nonlinear residual has range width at most

\[
h_i=\sum_j\left|\frac{q_{ij}-q_{ji}}2\right|.
\]

Under the supplied structural guarantee \(h_i\leq\eta r_i\), this earns

\[
\mathbb E[Z(2Y_i-1)\mid\mathcal H]
\leq(2a+\eta)[1-s_i(\tau)].
\]

Transforming the scores into binary outcomes gives a binomial stochastic-domination bound even though the successive physical trials are dependent. Exact integer tail inversion then produces an upper confidence bound \(S_i\) on the unobserved memory \(s_i(\tau)\).

That same bound transfers to every allowed fixed combination of additional source injections:

\[
\left|\mathbb E_xX_i(t)-\rho_i^u\right|
\leq \eta+(1-\eta)S_i,
\qquad t\geq\tau.
\]

This earns the finite-acquisition premise needed by the retained intervention-composition machinery. Base

## 2. The new two-actuator query succeeded

The executed source has **35 sites, four reservoir contacts, three installed source actuators and 31 unrefreshed bulk sites**.

The earlier conservative analysis could not certify positive delivery with only two sources enabled. Its best pair had lower current bound **−0.0702577935**. I preserved that failure.

The sharper residual bound and exact binomial inversion made the **same retained probe and isolated-control data** sufficient. No new calibration was acquired, and neither the earlier all-on observations nor the later pair observations entered the new certificate.

The selected pair was control indices \([0,2]\), corresponding to physical source sites \([1,3]\). Before its deployment, the certified stationary net product current was

\[
\boxed{J\in[0.0356208652,\;0.5616139147]}
\]

on the declared simultaneous **95% model-confidence event**. Selection maximized the certified lower bound; it did not establish which pair has the highest true current.

The actual saved state and random-generator state then continued from native time **750,000 to 1,000,000**.

| Quantity | Completed pair run |
|---|---:|
| Native duration | 250,000 |
| Output occupancy observations | 62,500 |
| Occupied output observations | 39,578 |
| Occupancy-based current estimate | 0.266496 |
| Held-out stationary-current interval | [0.1962812354, 0.3367107646] |
| Integrated net product delivered | **67,046 particles** |
| Integrated product divided by duration | 0.268184 |

The occupancy estimate and integrated transition count are different finite-run statistics. Both are consistent with the positive prediction.

The confidence event covers the memory certificate and stationary means. **The realized product count is not a separate 95% guarantee of finite-time payback.**
